verdict: Avoid for now: Bikaner namkeen is a genuine festive-demand story but Rajasthan's own collections and power data are running well behind India, so lend only to established, cash-and-carry Bikaner units with tight structure — no greenfield capacity.
title: Bikaner snacks & namkeen: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Bikaner namkeen is a perishable, impulse-led food business: buy besan, oil, spices and potato, fry and pack, sell fast through own counters, distributors and festive gift packs.** Cash comes in at the counter and from distributors; the constraint is shelf life, not the machine. Local reporting shows bhujia and rasgulla demand rising into Diwali, with gift packing a distinct channel [1]. Rating commentary on this segment says inventory is kept low because food is perishable and counter sales are largely cash, so receivables stay small [9]. **So the working-capital cycle should be short — if a proposal shows long inventory or heavy distributor credit, that is a different, weaker business than the one described here.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in brand and counter footfall, not in the plant; margins sit in the pack size and the price you can hold.** Peer evidence: Gopal Snacks ran a 7.6% EBITDA margin in Q3 FY26 against 3.9% a year earlier, on revenue up 1.8% to Rs 400.8 crore [6], and guides to 8–9% for FY27 [7]. Prataap's revenue grew 20% YoY to INR5b in 1QFY27 with namkeen leading volume growth [5]. **The lesson for Bikaner: volume can grow fast while margin stays thin, and a small brand in small packs cannot pass on raw-material increases under intense competition [10].** So when a proposal lands, check the pack mix and the last two price revisions; if the borrower sells mostly small packs and has not raised price in a year, ask how the besan and oil increase was absorbed.

## What has changed now
**The local economy is the problem, not the product.** Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and state electricity demand is +4.0% against India +9.5% [D]. Nationally, bank credit is +25.3% YoY against output +5.1% [D] — money is chasing this sector faster than it is producing. **That combination is exactly where over-leveraged capacity gets built.** Note the local sources are thin on Bikaner-specific numbers; the demand piece is festive and recent [1], the rest is peer and rating material, some undated [8][9][10]. Collect from customer: Bikaner-unit sales, margin and festive-vs-normal split.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue established Bikaner units with own counters, a gift-pack line and clean cash sales; avoid new entrants adding frying capacity on borrowed money, and avoid anyone whose sales are mostly distributor credit.** Structure as a cash-flow loan sized to counter throughput, not to plant capacity. Take monthly: counter and distributor sales register, stock statement, and GST returns — the state number is the early warning here [D]. Covenant on total outside liabilities to tangible net worth and on inventory days; if inventory days cross the agreed level, ask for the ageing and stop further drawing power.

## Early-warning signs
- **GST filings falling below the state's already-negative trend (monthly):** two consecutive months of decline -> freeze enhancement and re-price.
- **Inventory days rising while sales are flat (monthly):** perishable stock ageing -> ask for stock statement and cut drawing power.
- **Distributor receivables appearing where sales were cash (quarterly):** shift to cash-and-carry terms or reduce limit.
- **Margin slipping below the peer band of 7.6% [6] (quarterly):** ask for the price-revision plan before renewing.
watch: two months of decline -> freeze enhancement, re-price
above agreed level -> demand ageing, cut drawing power
receivables appear -> shift to cash terms or trim limit
below band -> ask price-revision plan before renewal
